short: The California Privacy Protection Agency's regulations under the CCPA add rules for automated decision-making technology used in significant decisions, mandatory risk assessments, and cybersecurity audits. They took effect January 1, 2026, with the ADMT duties phased to January 1, 2027.
title: CCPA Automated Decision-Making Technology Regulations
subtitle: California's privacy regulator rules on ADMT, risk assessments and cybersecurity audits, in force from 2026
body_html:
What the regulations are

The California Privacy Protection Agency adopted a package of regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act covering three subjects: automated decision-making technology, risk assessments, and cybersecurity audits. The agency's board approved the final text in July 2025, the Office of Administrative Law approved it on September 22, 2025, and the regulations took effect on January 1, 2026. They bind every business already subject to the CCPA.

This is the California rule that reaches AI through privacy law rather than through an AI-specific statute, which is why it sits beside the California AI laws page rather than inside it.

What it covers

  • ADMT in significant decisions. Technology that replaces or substantially replaces human decision-making about a consumer's finances, housing, education, employment, health care or essential goods and services. A business using it must give a pre-use notice, offer an opt-out (with exceptions where a human appeal is offered or the use is for security, fraud or safety), and respond to access requests explaining the logic and the output. These duties apply from January 1, 2027.
  • Risk assessments. Required before processing that presents significant risk to privacy, including selling or sharing personal information, processing sensitive data, using ADMT for a significant decision, and training ADMT or facial recognition on personal information. Processing that began before 2026 and continues must be assessed by December 31, 2027, and the first attestations and summaries are due to the agency by April 1, 2028.
  • Cybersecurity audits. Annual independent audits for larger businesses, phased by revenue from 2028 to 2030.

What changed in the final text

Earlier drafts reached behavioral advertising and any technology that facilitated a human decision. The final rule narrowed ADMT to technology that replaces or substantially replaces human judgment, dropped the advertising use case, and removed several notice elements. Readers who planned against the 2024 drafts should recheck scope.

Enforcement

The agency and the California Attorney General both enforce the CCPA. Administrative fines run to $2,500 per violation and $7,500 per intentional violation or violation involving a minor, per consumer. There is no private right of action for these provisions.

Related laws

The Colorado ADMT rulemaking under SB 26-189 covers similar ground by statute. The EU AI Act's high-risk categories and the GDPR Article 22 right overlap the significant-decision concept; see GDPR and AI. NYC Local Law 144 is the employment-only precedent.

Primary sources
